page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, utilizing simultaneous multithreading with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with a dedicated CPU allocation and provides 16.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a 1.0 GB per vCPU ratio. No local storage or GPUs are included in this configuration.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance placing in the top 25% at 2693.38. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth benchmarks fall within the average range, with a multi-core stress-ng score of 21558.27 and uncached read memory bandwidth of 75.4 GB/sec. Cryptographic and integer operations are supported by hardware-accelerated instructions like AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, though the processor lacks AVX-512 support.

The n2d-highcpu-16 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints. By limiting memory allocation to 1.0 GB per core, it reduces resource overhead while maintaining dedicated CPU performance. This configuration is suitable for workloads such as web serving, software compilation, and lightweight text or image processing.
